claim: Athena can time out on tables with many thousands of partitions that are not of type string. With type string it prunes partitions at the metastore level; with other types it prunes on the server side, which is slower.
question: Why can Athena time out on tables with many partitions, and what is the fix?

values.display: Athena prunes partitions at the metastore level

qualifiers.scope: tables with many thousands of partitions

evidence.quote: Timeouts on tables with many partitions – Athena may time out when querying a table that has many thousands of partitions. This can happen when the table has many partitions that are not of type string. When you use type string, Athena prunes partitions at the metastore level. However, when you use other data types, Athena prunes partitions on the server side.

claim: Athena treats source files that start with an underscore or a dot as hidden. To work around this, rename the files.
question: Why does Athena skip some files in an S3 location?

values.display: source files that start with an underscore

evidence.quote: Files treated as hidden – Athena treats source files that start with an underscore (_) or a dot (.) as hidden. To work around this limitation, rename the files.
